_strings.@@2d781e797ced: Personal Tax Credits (age 65+, blind, or Kentucky National Guard) — Taxpayer (and spouse, if filing jointly or married filing separately on a combined return) who, as of 12/31/2023, was age 65 or older, was legally blind, and/or was a member of the Kentucky National Guard. A taxpayer can claim more than one (e.g., 65+ AND blind). No income limit.
_strings.@@410d4e1e5215: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Residents who qualified for and claimed the federal child and dependent care credit on federal Form 2441 (care expenses for a qualifying child/dependent so the taxpayer can work). If you did not meet federal filing requirements but would have been entitled to the federal credit, you may still claim the Kentucky credit by completing federal Form 2441 and noting 'did not meet federal filing requirements.' Kentucky has no separate income limit; eligibility tracks the federal credit.

_strings.@@7d62ef21d9f6: 2023 Kentucky Individual Income Tax Forms — Form 740 Instruction Packet (42A740(PKT) (10-23)): "STANDARD DEDUCTION — For 2023, the standard deduction is $2,980" (ONE $2,980 per joint return; $2,980 each column when married filing separately on a combined return); Line 5 = Federal Adjusted Gross Income; Line 9 = Kentucky AGI; Line 11 = Taxable Income; Line 12 "Multiply line 11 by four and one-half percent (.045)".
_strings.@@e9a88c063d45: Treaty conformity — KY conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from KY income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the KY return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Kentucky's resident return (Form 740) starts from federal adjusted gross income — Form 740 line 5 is "Federal Adjusted Gross Income," and the 2023 740 instruction packet states: "Kentucky law requires that the individual income tax return begin with federal adjusted gross income and be adjusted for any differences to arrive at Kentucky adjusted gross income." Modifications are made on Schedule M. The Schedule M "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (lines 1-5) are: (1) interest on other states' obligations / mutual-fund dividends, (2) resident adjustment from KY Schedule K-1, (3) special depreciation/Section 179, (4) federal NOL, and (5) "other additions" (reservist/National Guard expenses, lump-sum distribution 20% capital-gains portion, passive activity loss adjustment, pension/IRA basis differences, intangible-asset gain differences). NONE of these add back federally tax-treaty-exempt income. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and KY has no add-back for it, it is not re-taxed by Kentucky — therefore KY conforms.

_strings.@@ff9566251a85: Family Size Tax Credit — Resident individuals/families with modified gross income (MGI) at or below 133% of the federal poverty threshold for their family size. Family size is capped at 4 (yourself, spouse if living in same household, and qualifying children). Available even to someone claimed as a dependent on a parent's return (family size 1). To get ANY credit, 2023 MGI must be at or below $19,391 (family of 1), $26,228 (family of 2), $33,064 (family of 3), or $39,900 (family of 4+).

Line 5 starts from federal AGI ("Do not confuse federal adjusted gross income with federal taxable income"). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Kentucky allows ONE $2,980 standard deduction per return — a joint return gets a single $2,980 (it is NOT doubled); spouses filing separately on a combined return get $2,980 each column. Kentucky has no personal or dependent exemptions; the nonrefundable personal tax credits (65-or-older, blind, National Guard) and the Family Size Tax Credit are NOT shipped (amounts unverified — see the comment above this block) and are NOT modeled by calc.state_tax.
